 Lane Kiffin is 6-4 in his first season at LSU — not exactly what Tigers fans were expecting. Stephen Lew / Imagn Images 
 By Joe Rexrode Nov. 16, 2026 6:00 am EST Updated Share article 84 Maybe it’s because even coaches and fans of winning teams are complaining about something in the college football universe, but 2026 seems like an especially sad season.
 Who’s truly happy? Who in Power 4 leagues is exceeding or even fully meeting expectations? UCLA. Wake Forest. Utah. I guess throw Alabama in there, especially because the College Football Playoff committee doesn’t recognize its 16-point loss at Tennessee. Great stories such as Kentucky and Oklahoma State have faded. Indiana is right there again , but you can’t call this a fully satisfying season for the Hoosiers.
 Advertisement
 The discontented are much more plentiful, and I’ve got five fanbases that stand atop the list. Talk close losses all you want, but LSU can’t find this debut season for Lane Kiffin acceptable. Dabo Swinney and Clemson just got throttled at home by a bad Georgia Tech team, and that’s a special run headed for a brutal ending. The Kyle Whittingham debut at Michigan is far worse than anyone reasonably could have imagined.
 Nebraska is a pretty good football team with no reason to believe it will ever make the right moves late in a big game against a good team while Matt Rhule is coaching . Texas A&M’s plummet has been precipitous, and Mike Elko has gone from adult in the room to profuse apologizer, especially skilled at dodging quarterback questions.
 Apologies to many other tremendous contenders. But Message Board Monday is taking those five teams and having a little contest for the saddest post. Prioritizing despair over anger. (Note: Some posts edited for grammar and length.)
 Cd104 on LSU: “Even how impressive Lane Kiffin’s last year was at Ole Miss, if we’re being real his schedule was not that difficult last year. Kiffin’s big game record is alarmingly bad. There’s years of evidence to unfortunately confirm he doesn’t get it done in big games. We’re stuck with him with that contract. Hopefully he turns it around but there’s no way to spin it, his first year was an utter disaster and nobody can defend this. It’s going to be a long, frustrating offseason and we are going to be slandered. We’ve gotta be the worst sports villians ever. Sports villains usually win. We have a losing SEC record.”
 Advertisement
 Cmastrangelom on Michigan: “My yard has never looked better. My garage is clean. Since my heart and spirit were broken (even before the Michigan State game), I can no longer be hurt by this Michigan team. Fire Kyle Whittingham. Lose a bunch of players I liked to the portal. Start over. It’s inevitable. Any other outcome will only prolong this disaster. For the moment I am delighted to be called a basketball school.”
 Winners and Losers: Bachelor U and Airplanes Manny Navarro and Jeshua Kidd A thread on Dabo Swinney started by Warlock and titled: “The first thing that made you fall in love with Dabo.” 
 Warlock: “For me it was hearing of how he told the board of directors something to the effect of ‘With all due respect, I don’t want us to be like Michigan and Alabama and Ohio State. I want them to want to be like us.’ This was, I believe, around the time the interim tag was removed.”
 JTJohnson: “His enthusiasm. At the time, it felt like our program was stale and lifeless. And now, symmetry.”
 Howard’s Jock: “Strange thread is strange. I never cared for his personality. But I liked the winning.”
 CU1998: “Surely you’ve been to a funeral. I was skeptical of Dabo when hired. But his conviction to all things is what grabbed me. Not ashamed at all of what he led Clemson football to or how he led it there.”
 Advertisement
 Teecue on Nebraska: “My question is, what is the selling point to the fans for next year? What are we supposed to see that makes us believe year 5 under Matt Rhule will be any different? I assume the biggest thing we’ll hear about is the new OC. Maybe I’m too skeptical, but Rhule’s offenses have looked pretty similar everywhere he’s been regardless of who the OC is. Then there’s the money. We’re top 20 nationally and sixth in the Big Ten. If that investment produces the result we are seeing now, I don’t think anyone can argue the resources.
 “And now we’re committing even more. Rhule already has a massive buyout. The DC just got extended. We’ve committed money to bring our QB back next year, and I don’t think his play this season has matched that investment. How does Nebraska sell this to the fans? Buy your tickets, spend more money on this program, continue the sellout streak. Believe things will be different because … why?”
 A thread started by 1command on Texas A&M and titled: “I’m 58 years old.” 
 1command: “And I’m pretty much set in concrete that I won’t see an Aggie football natty. We probably won’t even be in the new 24-team Playoff any time soon.”
 Mr jingles: “Pretty much? Guarantee? A&M’s football fate has been sealed forever.”
 Goose77: “Totally agree. Everyone look in the mirror tonight and just accept it. We. Will. Never. Win. Ever. Now, go enjoy your lives.”
 Dirkieduck: “At 55 I had hope, at 65 more hope, at 75 pretty sure, at 85 hell yes. At 86 — poop!”
 A truly melancholy menagerie, but the wistful reminiscing about Swinney wins the day. Kiffin has been bad in big games, but coaches have figured that out before and he’ll have his opportunities. Michigan just has to get its next hire (whenever that may be) right. The hopelessness is a bit deeper at Nebraska and Texas A&M.
 But Swinney is one of the greatest things to happen to Clemson, and it’s painfully obvious where this is heading. It’s mid-November, the most important games of the college football season lie ahead, and Clemson fans are thumbing through the old family photo album with moist eyes.
